name: Bhimeswara Swamy Temple, Draksharamam
deity: Shiva worshipped as Bhimeswara; consort Manikyamba, revered as one of the eighteen Ashtadasha Shakti Peethas
dynasty: Eastern Chalukya (great mandapam added by Ganga Mahadevi)
summary: One of the five Pancharama Kshetras, Draksharama enshrines Shiva as Bhimeswara in a towering crystal linga — and, as a Shakti Peetha of the goddess Manikyamba, holds the Godavari delta's holiest ground where Sun and Sati are remembered together.

sections.history: Draksharama's Bhimeswara temple was raised by the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi between the 9th and 10th centuries CE, and tradition credits its building to King Bhima, whose name the presiding Shiva still bears. A later benefactor, Ganga Mahadevi, is remembered for the great pillared mandapam that enlarged the shrine. But the temple's deeper claim on history is written into its own walls: Draksharama is among the greatest epigraphic sites of Andhra, its enclosures crowded with early Telugu and Sanskrit inscriptions that record centuries of royal gifts, land grants and endowments. To read those stones is to trace the medieval life of the delta — the Chalukyas of Vengi, the Cholas who married into them, and the Kakatiya, Reddi and Vijayanagara rulers who followed all left their mark here. Few temples in the south preserve so continuous a documentary record, and for historians of Telugu the temple is a foundational archive as much as a place of worship.
sections.architecture: The temple is built on two storeys and set within two concentric, fort-like enclosure walls that give it the aspect of a walled citadel of faith. Its heart is the linga of Bhimeswara — an exceptionally tall shaft rising about 2.6 metres, roughly 8.5 feet, and described as a single crystal, or spatika, linga whose upper portion shines white. That white crown is understood to embody the Ardhanareeswara principle, Shiva and Shakti conjoined in one form. Because the linga stands so high, priests offer worship not from the floor but from an upper gallery that brings the devotee level with the deity's face — a rare and memorable arrangement. Water for the daily abhisheka is drawn from the Sapta Godavari Kundam, the sacred tank believed to be fed by the seven underground streams of the Godavari, so that the river itself bathes the god. The Dravidian plan carries the blended Chalukya–Chola manner of the delta.
sections.legends: Two great stories meet at Draksharama. In the first, the linga here is one of the five fragments of the Pancharama legend: the asura Tarakasura wore an invincible Shiva linga, and when Kartikeya could not slay him, Vishnu revealed the linga must be broken. Shattered by the fire weapon, it fell in five pieces that chanted 'Om' and sought to reunite; each was fixed where it landed, and Draksharama is one of these five kshetras. Local tradition adds that the Sun god Surya himself installed and worshipped the linga here. The second story makes Draksharama a Shakti Peetha — one of the eighteen — where a part of the goddess Sati is said to have fallen; she is venerated as Manikyamba, so the temple is at once a Shiva kshetra and a seat of the Mother.
sections.festivals: Maha Shivaratri is the temple's principal festival, when the delta streams toward Draksharama through a night of vigil and worship. Kalyanotsavam, the ceremonial marriage of Bhimeswara and Manikyamba, is celebrated with special splendour, fitting a temple that is both Shiva kshetra and Shakti Peetha. The month of Kartika is intensely observed, its Kartika Purnima drawing lamp-lit crowds, while Dasara or Navaratri honours the goddess Manikyamba across nine nights. Festival days extend the temple's hours and fill its enclosures.
sections.experience: To visit Draksharama is to feel two devotions at once — the Shaiva and the Shakta — held within a single ancient enclosure. Climb to the upper gallery to stand level with the towering crystal linga, a perspective few temples offer, and let your eye travel the crowded inscriptions that turn the walls into a library of stone. Pause at the Sapta Godavari Kundam, where the hidden river is said to surface, before circling the Manikyamba shrine. The town sits deep in the Konaseema delta, green with paddy and coconut, about 28 km from Kakinada — an unhurried, deeply local pilgrimage far from the tourist circuit.

visit.timings: Generally open daily around 6 am to 12 noon and again from 4 pm to 8 pm; festival days, especially Maha Shivaratri and the month of Kartika, extend these hours considerably.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — sarees or salwar for women, dhoti or shirt and trousers for men; footwear is left outside before entering the enclosures.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer areas and courtyards but not inside the inner sanctum; follow posted signs and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Draksharamam lies in the Konaseema district of Andhra Pradesh, about 28 km from Kakinada and 25 km from Amalapuram. The nearest railheads are Kakinada, Samalkot Junction and Rajahmundry; the nearest airport is Rajahmundry (RJA), about 50 km away, with Visakhapatnam a larger alternative. Roads run through the Godavari delta.
